headline: Kai, the US struck Iran again while claiming progress in talks, days after de-escalation hopes handed oil its steepest weekly slide since COVID.
subline: A gunman killed at least five in Kraków's Main Square, Senate control starts resolving this week, and October CPI lands Tuesday morning.
asof: Weekend edition · built Sunday ~6:45 AM ET · strip shows Friday's close; bitcoin is live · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Brent just logged its steepest week since COVID
items.sentence: Brent settled Friday at $98.32 after a 13% weekly slide built on hopes of US-Iran de-escalation — a bet now tested by the weekend's new strikes — per Hammerstone Markets' recap on Investrade.

items.title: Bitcoin rides out the weekend above $75,000
items.sentence: Bitcoin sits at $75,813 Sunday morning, down about 3% on the week and 39.9% below its $126,080 all-time high, with CoinGecko flagging ETF outflows and Binance hack fallout as the drags.

items.title: Consumer mood improves as inflation expectations cool
items.sentence: Michigan's preliminary November consumer sentiment jumped to 51.0 from October's 48.0 while one-year inflation expectations eased to 4.3% from 4.7%, per Hammerstone's Friday recap on Investrade.

items.title: Susquehanna: 40% of planned data centers at risk
items.sentence: Susquehanna estimates 60 gigawatts of planned 2025-2030 AI data-center projects — roughly 40% — are at risk of delay under the incoming Democratic Congress, per the Hammerstone recap on Investrade.

items.title: Week ahead: October CPI lands Tuesday
items.sentence: October CPI arrives Tuesday at 8:30 AM ET as the week's main event, with Fed speakers and Treasury auctions stacked up Monday, per Thrive in Markets' calendar and Finwire's preview.

items.title: US launches new targeted strikes on Iran
items.sentence: The US launched new targeted strikes on Iran even as President Trump claimed progress in talks with Tehran, per Euronews.

items.title: Gunman kills at least five in Kraków
items.sentence: A gunman firing from a passing car into the Main Square killed at least five people and wounded more than a dozen before police shot him, per Euronews, whose updated headline puts the toll at six.

items.title: Senate control narrows to mail and math
items.sentence: Scott Colom leads Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 2,574 votes in Mississippi, where mail ballots must arrive by Tuesday, and Mary Peltola's 637-vote Alaska lead heads to ranked-choice tabulation on Nov. 18, per AP counts in Yahoo News' live blog.

items.title: Stephen Miller to run the White House
items.sentence: Trump said Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff starting Monday, a post-rout shake-up drawing criticism from Democrats and some Republicans, per Yahoo News' live blog.

items.title: Eisenkot gets first shot at Israeli coalition
items.sentence: Israel's president tapped Gadi Eisenkot, Benjamin Netanyahu's strongest rival, to try to form a government after a deadlocked election left neither man a clear path to power, per Reuters via Yahoo News.

items.title: OpenAI's trimmed $11 billion round reported closed
items.sentence: A Saturday brief citing Bloomberg and Reuters reports OpenAI closed an $11 billion round at a $1.25 trillion valuation, trimmed from earlier targets, though some roundups still call the figures unconfirmed, per Tech Trends News Update.

items.title: Mistral opens weights on a trillion-parameter model
items.sentence: Mistral has released open weights for Large 4, its 1-trillion-parameter multimodal flagship, though model-resellers need a separate commercial license, per Lets Data Science.

items.title: Thinking Machines circles a $40 billion valuation
items.sentence: Thinking Machines Lab is reportedly in talks to raise $5 billion to $6 billion at a pre-money valuation of at least $40 billion — Accel leading, Nvidia in for about $2.5 billion — per Industry.co.id's AI roundup.

items.title: Anthropic adds watermarks to older Claude models
items.sentence: RUDI's digest, citing Mezha, reports Anthropic is applying machine-readable watermarks to output from older Claude models across its products and API with no customer opt-out, ahead of an EU AI Act deadline in December.

items.title: Bombay court tosses order citing AI-invented judgments
items.sentence: The Bombay High Court quashed a customs order and sent it back for a fresh hearing after the petitioner showed it relied on two untraceable, apparently AI-hallucinated Supreme Court judgments, per RUDI's digest citing LawChakra.
